Anna — thanks for laying this out. High level answers below and attaching a concise data-flow diagram (redwood-eu-data-flow.pdf). Happy to run through on a call — proposing Thu 29 Jul 10:00 CET.

Quick answers:
- EU-only processing: Our Redbox (private control plane for Private deployments) will run inference and persistent storage in the chosen EU region (we currently offer eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). Runtime routing policy pins requests to the in-region pool; fallback to non-EU pools occurs only under operator-declared emergency policies and is disabled by default for Private accounts.
- KMS & keys: Customer-managed CMKs supported via KMS integrations (we can use your KMS in-region or Redwood-managed KMS with region-scoped keys). Key material for customer CMKs never leaves the configured region.
- Backups: Snapshots are region-local; by default backups are kept for 30 days. We can configure retention per customer down to 0 days for snapshots. Deletion proof: we produce SHA256 manifests of deleted objects and retention metadata plus a timestamped audit event.
- Personnel access: Access is role-based and logged. Only a small set of engineers in the Infra/Private-ops team have break-glass access and such access requires a documented approval workflow and audit.
- Subprocessors: For Private deployments we do not route data through third-party cloud connectors outside the customer's region. For Dedicated/Hosted we have a small set of cloud partners; list will be provided in the SCCs annex.

I attached the high-level flow and will follow up with technical specifics (backup lifecycle, KMS key residency, audit log extract examples). If Thu 10:00 CET works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Technical clarifications for Anna / MediCorp legal:
- Backups & snapshots: snapshots are stored in-region; however, automated cross-region replication is an optional feature that is disabled for EU-only configs. If you want to be extra conservative we will disable replication and set snapshot TTL to 0 days post-provisioning.
- Persistent caches (KV-cache): ephemeral by design; cache eviction is deterministic and we can flush KV caches on customer request.
- Logs & audit events: control-plane logs (rollouts, operator actions) can be routed to your customer-managed logging bucket in-region. Access to control-plane logs is governed by the same RBAC and requires privileged approvals.
- SCCs operationalization: we implement SCCs via contractual annex + technical controls: processor-subprocessor mapping, limited access, encryption at rest in-region, and documented standing instructions. The attached workbook annotates where each SCC clause maps to our controls.

Attaching: SCCs-annotation.xlsx (spreadsheet with clause->control mapping), redwood-eu-data-flow.pdf (data flow diagram).
